points.description: States that the statement is FALSE.

Justification: the OS can use system calls as events/opportunities (entry into the kernel) to switch between processes / run the scheduler, so it can schedule READY processes without the timer interrupt.
points.partial_credit: Only if clearly more than half: says the OS can switch on events such as system calls or blocking/yielding, but without naming system calls precisely.

points.description: States that without the timer interrupt scheduling is not fair (no preemption/fair CPU sharing), but the OS can still schedule different processes.

rubric.notes: Full marks need FALSE, system calls named as the event that lets the OS switch processes, and the point that execution is unfair without the timer but scheduling still works. A TRUE answer, or no correct justification, gets 0 overall. Vague justifications such as 'OS has other ways' without system calls earn nothing on P2.
